messages:
Jordan Patel: Heads-up — customer reporting intermittent 503s and very high p95 for /v1/generate. Can you confirm what minimal artifacts we need to triage quickly?
Priya Nair: For fast repro+escalation we usually ask for: request header snapshot (including any x-* ids), full response status & body, a short curl that reproduces failure, app logs around the timestamp, and a screenshot of the Console session view.
Omar Liu: +1. Specific headers we look for: `x-rw-request-id`, `x-debug-token` (if present), `x-forwarded-for`, and `authorization` (ask them to redact the token). If the SDK is used, mention `sessionId` / `sdkTraceId` fields.
Priya Nair: If the customer can’t share full logs, ask for the single request window (10s before/after) and the exact client timestamp. Also request the p95/p99 numbers they see and the local CLI/curl latency.
Omar Liu: Example minimal curl to ask for (they should replace placeholders):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "x-rw-request-id: <copy-from-client-headers>" \
  -H "x-debug-token: <if-available>" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-l1","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --compressed
```
Jordan Patel: Nice. Also tell them how to grab the Console debug token: Console -> Sessions -> click the session -> Debug token (top-right) -> `Copy debug token`. If they are on a managed Dedicated/Private instance, say where the session link appears in their org UI.
Priya Nair: For mobile SDKs: ask for the SDK log snippet that shows the outbound request headers (look for `sendRequest` / `fetch` logs), and whether any proxy or WAF sits in front of Redwood. If they use our JS SDK ask them to enable `RW_SDK_DEBUG=1` for one run.
tracebot: Debug token generated: dt_9f3a2b (use with `x-debug-token` header)
Omar Liu: If they can’t run curl, a HAR export from the browser is fine — ask for the entry with the POST to `/v1/generate` and to include the request + response tabs.
Jordan Patel: Final customer message to send (copy/paste):
"Hi — to help us reproduce the 503s please send: 1) the `x-rw-request-id` value from one failing request; 2) a curl that reproduces the call (example below); 3) the full response (status + body) and a HAR or SDK log snippet; 4) the Console debug token if available (Console -> Sessions -> Debug token). Please redact Authorization before sending."
Priya Nair: Add: timestamp (UTC) when the failure happened and their regional endpoint (us-east-1/eu-west-1). That helps us find the server trace quickly.
Omar Liu: After they send, attach the request id to the internal escalation ticket and ping `@eng-runtime` with the id and debug token. We can pull the trace from our side.
Jordan Patel: Thanks — I’ll send this to the customer now and update the ticket with anything they send back. :thumbsup:
